paragraph: [Novo Jornal reported on 23 January 2026](<https://www.novojornal.co.ao/politica/detalhe/proposta-de-lei-de-ciberseguranca-aprovada-mas-com-a-abstencao-da-unita-que-receia-que-governo-recorra-ao-corte-de-internet-nos-dias-das-eleicoes-e-das-manifestacoes-69381.html>) that a UNITA deputy called Law 7/17 of 16 February part of the current legal order. The law covers the protection of computer networks and systems. In the last twelve months the Assembly [adopted the new cybersecurity law on 12 August 2026](<https://angop.ao/fr/noticias/economia/angola-conta-com-lei-sobre-ciberseguranca/>), which the deputy said would repeal Law 7/17. Angola's minister said it [has entered into force](<https://www.sadc.int/latest-news/sadc-strengthens-regional-cybersecurity-and-cybercrime-cooperation>), as SADC reported on 16 October 2026. No arrest, charge, prosecution, conviction or penalty has been found in the last three years. Operating would need a dated arrest, charge, prosecution or conviction, or a penalty.

Burundi's cybercrime law is [Law No. 1/10 of 16 March 2022 on the prevention and repression of cybercrime](<https://communityvoice.bi/1489-2/>). In the last twelve months it was cited and not changed. At a workshop in Bujumbura in February 2026 a government delegate called it adopted and in application. Participants discussed its gaps against the Malabo Convention. No arrest, charge, prosecution, conviction or penalty has been found in the last three years. Operating would need a dated arrest, charge, prosecution or conviction, or a penalty.

Benin's [Loi n° 2017-20 of 20 April 2018, the Code du numérique](<https://sgg.gouv.bj/doc/loi-2017-20/download>), treats illegal access to and penetration of an information system as offences in its Livre VI. No change to the code has been found in the last twelve months. Benin's Centre national d'investigations numériques [reported over 6,500 digital-offence complaints in 2025](<https://africaho.bj/article/infractions-en-ligne-au-benin-ce-que-revele-le-bilan-2025-du-cnin/>), and [INTERPOL's Operation Sentinel](<https://www.interpol.int/en/News-and-Events/News/2025/574-arrests-and-USD-3-million-recovered-in-coordinated-cybercrime-operation-across-Africa>) led to 106 arrests in Benin between 27 October and 27 November 2025. Neither source names the code. Operating would need a dated arrest, charge, prosecution or conviction naming the law, or a penalty.

Burkina Faso's [Loi n°014-2024/ALT of 9 July 2024](<https://www.an.bf/storage/libelrapportautres/rXFCav065KRZXiB2PB65xip11Qg8fPpCZ3sjGpsf.pdf>) sets rules to control and protect information systems, with licensing and fines. In the last twelve months the Council of Ministers of 30 July 2026 [adopted decrees applying it](<https://burkina24.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/CONSEIL-DES-MINISTRES-N%C2%B025-DU-30-JUILLET-2026.pdf>). One categorises critical-infrastructure bodies, and the other sets security audits and auditor accreditation. The cybercrime brigade [arrested two people in August 2025](<https://burkina24.com/2025/08/14/lutte-contre-la-cybercriminalite-deux-individus-arretes-pour-usurpation-de-fonction-et-diffamation-en-ligne/>) and [22 people in October 2025](<https://ouaga24.com/operation-cyber-balayage-2025-22-interpellations-et-plus-de-18-millions-fcfa-de-prejudice/>). Neither source names the 2024 law. Operating would need a dated arrest, charge, prosecution or conviction naming the law, or a penalty.

Botswana's Cybersecurity Act, 2025 (Act No. 21 of 2025) was [assented to on 5 November 2025 and gazetted on 11 November 2025](<https://www.bocra.org.bw/sites/default/files/sites/default/files/documents/Cybersecurity_ACT_-_5%20Nov_2025.pdf>). It repeals and replaces the Cybercrime and Computer Related Crimes Act 2018, and takes effect on a date the Minister appoints by Order. In the last twelve months it was cited and not brought into force: in March 2026 the communications minister said it was [expected to come into force in April](<https://dailynews.gov.bw/news-detail/90463>). No order appointing a date has been found. No arrest, charge, prosecution, conviction or penalty has been found in the last three years. Operating would need a dated arrest, charge, prosecution or conviction, or a penalty.

The telecoms regulator ARCEP's index lists [Loi 24.002 of 21 February 2024 on cybersecurity and the fight against cybercrime](<https://www.arcep.cf/fr/index.php/reglementation/lois-et-ordonnances>) among the country's laws. The National Assembly had [voted the bill by acclamation on 25 January 2024](<https://www.africatopsuccess.com/un-projet-de-loi-pour-lutter-contre-la-cybercriminalite-en-centrafrique/>). No change to the law has been found in the last twelve months. An [opinion piece of 18 August 2026](<https://corbeaunews-centrafrique.org/cybercriminalite-a-saint-petersbourg-evariste-ngamana-defend-un-combat-perdu-davance-contre-les-reseaux-sociaux/>) refers to it as wielded by the prosecutor's office and police. No arrest, charge, prosecution, conviction or penalty has been found in the last three years. Operating would need a dated arrest, charge, prosecution or conviction, or a penalty.

Côte d'Ivoire's cybercrime law is [law no. 2013-451 of 19 June 2013, amended by law no. 2023-593 of 7 June 2023](<https://www.linfodrome.com/societe/126588-cybersecurite-en-cote-d-ivoire-l-anssi-la-sentinelle-du-cyberespace-ivoirien>). [In October 2025 a man was prosecuted under the 2013 law](<https://www.aip.ci/cote-divoire-aip-cybercriminalite-un-marabout-arrete-pour-arnaque-et-chantage-sur-son-ami-a-abidjan/>) for threatening to spread sexual images. The national information-security agency's platform [received and handled 12,100 files in 2024](<https://www.fratmat.info/article/2634113/societe/cybercriminalite-en-cote-divoire-12-100-dossiers-traites-pour-un-prejudice-de-7-milliards-de-fcfa>), and the report as relayed does not name the law. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found shows the law in regular use in the last two years. Mature would need sources from the past two years that show it used again and again.

Cameroon's cybercrime law is [Law no. 2010/012 of 21 December 2010](<https://lejour.cm/cameroun-quand-les-lois-sur-la-cybercriminalite-menacent-les-libertes/>), which a June 2026 Le Jour report treats as the existing law. In the last twelve months it was cited and not changed. A workshop in Yaounde on 8 and 9 June 2026 reviewed its articles. A [Nkafu brief of 4 September 2026](<https://nkafu.org/cybersecurity-as-industrial-policy-protecting-cameroons-digital-economy/>) called for it to be revised. No arrest, charge, prosecution, conviction or penalty has been found in the last three years. Operating would need a dated arrest, charge, prosecution or conviction, or a penalty.

The Democratic Republic of the Congo's cybercrime provisions sit in the [Code du numérique, Ordonnance-loi n° 23/010 of 13 March 2023](<https://acp.cd/economie/cybersecurite-un-atelier-de-validation-de-sept-arretes-lance-a-kinshasa/>). In the last twelve months, on 17 August 2026 the Attorney General at the Court of Cassation [told judicial police officers to take up offences under the Digital Code](<https://acp.cd/anglais/drc-judicial-police-officers-advised-to-prosecute-perpetrators-of-digital-offences/>) on their own initiative. In November 2026 ACP reported seven ministerial orders drafted to put the Code into effect. No arrest, charge, prosecution, conviction or penalty has been found in the last three years. Operating would need a dated arrest, charge, prosecution or conviction, or a penalty.

The Republic of the Congo has two laws of 5 June 2020, loi n° 26-2020 on cybersecurity and loi n° 27-2020 on the fight against cybercrime. The Journal officiel of [18 June 2026](<https://sgg.cg/JO/2026/congo-jo-2026-25.pdf>) prints a decree of 6 May 2026 that cites both as in force. In the last twelve months they were cited and not changed. In its 2025 assessment, [UNESCO](<https://www.unesco.org/fr/articles/evaluation-du-developpement-de-linternet-en-republique-du-congo>) says their application still has to be strengthened, and it cites no arrest, prosecution or conviction under either. Operating would need a dated arrest, charge, prosecution or conviction, or a penalty.

The Comoros promulgated its [new Penal Code by decree on 16 February 2021](<https://anaden.org/actualites/anaden-information-les-avancees-sur-le-code-numerique>), according to the national digital agency ANADEN. It is loi n°20-38/AU of 29 December 2020, and its articles 449 to 505 set out cybercrime offences. ANADEN's publication of 4 March 2021 lists a specific cybersecurity law as drafted and not yet adopted. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No case brought has been found in the last three years. Operating would need a dated arrest, charge, prosecution or conviction, or a penalty.

Cabo Verde has Decreto-lei n.º 9/2021, its cybersecurity regime, with Decreto-Regulamentar n.º 1/2021, which creates the national CSIRT. The [2026 State Budget law](<https://www.mf.gov.cv/documents/198414/5793427/Lei%20que%20aprova%20o%20OE%202026.pdf>) cites them as in place. No change to either decree has been found in the last twelve months. The [NOSi plan for 2024](<https://www.nosi.cv/documents/20121/2842828/PAO_2024.pdf>) lists them among existing texts, and neither document records a case brought under the law. Operating would need a dated arrest, charge, prosecution or conviction, or a penalty.

[Law n°66/AN/14/7ème L of 20 July 2014 on cybersecurity and the fight against cybercrime](<https://www.journalofficiel.dj/texte-juridique/loi-n-18-an-23-9eme-ll-portant-ratification-de-la-convention-de-lunion-africaine-sur-la-cybersecurite-et-la-protection-de-donnees-a-caractere-personnel/>) is cited by Djibouti's 2023 law ratifying the Malabo Convention. The National Assembly [passed a Digital Code on 30 June 2025](<https://www.jonesday.com/en/insights/2025/07/national-assembly-of-the-republic-of-djibouti-approves-digital-code>), with Book VI on cybersecurity and cybercrime, and its legislative section still awaited promulgation. No change to the 2014 law has been found in the last twelve months. No arrest, charge, prosecution, conviction or penalty under either text has been found in the last three years. Operating would need a dated arrest, charge, prosecution or conviction, or a penalty.

Algeria's [Law 09-04 of 5 August 2009](<https://www.joradp.dz/FTP/jo-francais/2020/F2020004.pdf>) sets rules on preventing and fighting offences linked to information and communication technologies. Presidential decree 20-05 of 20 January 2020 lists it among the laws it rests on. In the last twelve months, in March 2026 the director general of the security agency ASSI [announced a draft cybersecurity bill](<https://www.expressdz.dz/2026/03/03/mdn-le-contenu-de-la-strategie-nationale-de-la-securite-des-systemes-dinformation-2025-2029-devoile/>). It would make security measures mandatory for institutions. No arrest, charge, prosecution, conviction or penalty has been found in the last three years. Operating would need a dated arrest, charge, prosecution or conviction, or a penalty.

Egypt's cybercrime law is Law 175 of 2018 on combating information technology crimes. An Economic Court ruling of November 2025 [applies the law and its executive regulations](<https://www.egyptke.com/99712>), Prime Ministerial Decree 1699 of 2020. In the last twelve months, on 29 November 2025 the Cairo Economic Court [sentenced video blogger Mohamed Abdel Aaty to two years and a fine under the law](<https://ldsf.info/blog/2025/12/01/escalates-war-on-digital11225/>). It sentenced Qamar El-Wekala to six months. An MP's bill of 22 April 2026 [would tighten the law's provisions](<https://www.elwatannews.com/news/details/8270615>). [A second MP's bill](<https://www.elbalad.news/6945377>) would raise its penalties.

Eritrea has no separate cybercrime act. The [Council of Europe cybercrime office's legal profile](<https://rm.coe.int/octocom-legal-profile-eritrea/16809efad6>), in its version of 5 May 2020, maps the Penal Code to the Budapest Convention's offence articles. Article 374 covers unauthorized use of a computer, including access, interception, and data and system interference, and Article 298 covers violation of privacy. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No arrest, charge, prosecution, conviction or penalty has been found in the last three years. Operating would need a dated arrest, charge, prosecution or conviction, or a penalty.

Ethiopia's cybercrime law is [Computer Crime Proclamation No. 958/2016](<https://www.bbc.com/amharic/articles/c80lyxz1l1ko>). The Federal High Court applied it in November 2024 to find Meskerem Abera guilty on two counts over two YouTube programmes. In the last twelve months, [Birr Metrics reported in December 2025](<https://birrmetrics.com/ethiopian-high-court-frees-tiktok-streaming-passenger-and-co-defendants/>) that Yohanis Daniel faced an added charge under the law over a TikTok live stream. Proclamation No. 1426/2026 on critical infrastructure was [signed on 21 July 2026](<https://www.insa.gov.et/pdf/download/critical-infrastructure-cybersecurity-proclamation-no-14262026-1786083598>) and takes effect in July 2027. No source found shows the law in regular use in the last two years. Mature would need sources from the past two years that show it used again and again.

[Gabonreview, on 1 June 2025](<https://www.gabonreview.com/laninf-renforce-la-cybersecurite-nationale-avec-secbom/>), presented law no. 027/2023 on cybersecurity and the fight against cybercrime as a national law. ANINF's SecBOM tool must comply with it. In the last twelve months, [a law ratifying the ordinance on social networks was promulgated by decree 0436/PR of 5 October 2026](<https://gabonmediatime.com/gabon-amendes-jusqua-50-millions-et-peines-de-prison-pour-les-abus-commis-sur-les-reseaux-sociaux/>). It sets five years' imprisonment and a fine of FCFA 5 to 20 million for using another person's identifying details to deceive users. No arrest, charge, prosecution, conviction or penalty has been found in the last three years. Operating would need a dated arrest, charge, prosecution or conviction, or a penalty.

[Digital Policy Alert](<https://digitalpolicyalert.org/digest/dpa-digital-digest-ghana>) says Ghana's Cybersecurity Act of 2020 sets measures for critical infrastructure, cybercrime prevention and incident response. It created the Cyber Security Authority. In the last twelve months, in December 2025 the communications minister said [over 272 comments had come in](<https://techfocus24.com/communication-ministry-seeks-private-sector-input-on-cybersecurity-act/>) on a draft amendment bill. On 13 August 2026 the Graphic reported that the Authority [fined the Office of the Registrar of Companies GH¢240,000](<https://www.graphic.com.gh/news/general-news/office-of-registrar-of-companies-and-service-provider-fined-ghc240-000-for-breaches-cybersecurity-directive-breaches.html>) under Section 92. It also fined Purpleline Solutions Limited GH¢120,000. No source found shows the law in regular use in the last two years. Mature would need sources from the past two years that show it used again and again.

Guinea has had a law on cybersecurity and personal data protection [since 2016](<https://afrique-diplomatique.com/guinee-consultations-sur-la-revision-du-cadre-juridique-de-la-cybersecurite/>), mainly aimed at cybercrime, according to the director of ANSSI's alert centre. In the last twelve months, on 13 August 2026 ANSSI held a consultation workshop on draft texts on cybersecurity and cybercrime. They were prepared with SOCSLAWYERS to update the 2016 framework. On [26 July 2025](<https://aminata.com/guinee_loi-sur-la-cybersecurite-le-president-de-haute-autorite-de-la-communication-apporte-des-precisions/>) the media regulator's president said the law will be applied to web media that break the rules. No arrest, charge, prosecution, conviction or penalty has been found in the last three years. Operating would need a dated arrest, charge, prosecution or conviction, or a penalty.

The Gambia's [Information and Communications Act, 2009](<https://www.wipo.int/wipolex/en/legislation/details/10478>) (No. 2 of 2009) entered into force on 29 May 2009. Its Part III of Chapter III, on computer misuse and cyber crime, creates offences such as unauthorised access to computer data. Parliament introduced a Cybercrime Bill in March 2024. In the last twelve months the [Oxford Institute of Technology and Justice](<https://www.techandjustice.bsg.ox.ac.uk/thegambia-3447303d-c9d6-4476-963c-02898588dc35>) stated that, as at June 2026, it has not been enacted, and in [November 2026 the bill was reported still under debate](<https://alkambatimes.com/ai-is-arriving-in-the-gambia-are-we-ready-for-the-risks/>). No arrest, charge, prosecution, conviction or penalty has been found in the last three years. Operating would need a dated arrest, charge, prosecution or conviction, or a penalty.

On 1 July 2026 the Government [stated](<https://www.guineaecuatorialpress.com/noticias/el_gobierno_recuerda_la_plena_vigencia_de_la_ley_que_regula_el_uso_de_las_redes_sociales_los_delitos_informaticos_y_la_ciber_delincuencia>) that Ley 7/2024 is fully in force. The law dates from 23 December 2024 and covers social networks, computer crimes and cybercrime. In the last twelve months, on 16 September 2026 lawyers for vice-president Teodoro Nguema Obiang Mangue [lodged four private criminal complaints](<https://www.guineaecuatorialpress.com/noticias/el_despacho_que_representa_a_se_nguema_obiang_mangue_explica_las_acciones_contra_diadario_rombe_y_otras_tres_personas>) under it at a Malabo court. They await the court. No arrest, prosecutor's charge or court decision has been found. Operating would need a dated arrest, charge, prosecution or conviction, or a penalty.

Kenya's Computer Misuse and Cybercrimes Act of 2018 stands. The [Computer Misuse and Cybercrimes (Amendment) Act, 2025](<https://parliament.go.ke/sites/default/files/2025-10/Computer%20Misuse%20and%20Cybercrimes%20%28Amendment%29%20Act%2C%202025.pdf>) amended it from 4 November 2025. In the last twelve months, in March 2026 the Court of Appeal [struck down sections 22 and 23](<https://nation.africa/kenya/news/major-victory-as-court-declares-illegal-sections-of-cybercrimes-law-used-to-hunt-down-bloggers-activists-5382142>), its false-publication offences, and upheld the rest. CPJ reports that journalist Peter Mwita was [charged in a Mombasa court](<https://cpj.org/2026/02/kenya-court-due-to-rule-on-cybercrimes-law-as-another-journalist-faces-jail/>) in February 2026 and pleaded not guilty. On 3 September 2026 Kenya [launched an official guide](<https://www.the-star.co.ke/news/2026-09-03-kenya-rolls-out-new-cybercrime-playbook-as-digital-threats-grow>) to prosecuting 76 listed cyber offences under the Act.

[President Boakai approved Liberia's Cybercrime Act on 3 July 2026](<https://liberianinvestigator.com/dopoh-liberia-cybercrime-law-enforcement-safeguards/>). The House had passed it in 2023 and the Senate in November 2025. In the last twelve months, in September 2026 police [arrested the commentator Jerry Nyantee Wrato](<https://frontpageafricaonline.com/liberia-cdc-prepares-to-take-cybercrime-law-fight-to-supreme-court-after-wrato-release/>) over AI-generated images of the Vice President. The Inspector General's letter of 21 September resolved to prosecute him under [sections 10.1, 15.1, 18.1 and 19.1 of the Act](<https://allafrica.com/stories/202609240628.html>). A court ordered him released on habeas corpus on 22 September. No source found shows the law in regular use in the last two years. Mature would need sources from the past two years that show it used again and again.

[On 15 November 2026 a House committee discussed gaps in Libya's Law No. 5 of 2022 on combating cybercrime](<https://alwasat.ly/news/485128>). [Cabinet Decision 358 of 15 July 2026 cites it among its legal bases](<https://lawsociety.ly/legislation/%d9%82%d8%b1%d8%a7%d8%b1-%d9%85%d8%ac%d9%84%d8%b3-%d8%a7%d9%84%d9%88%d8%b2%d8%b1%d8%a7%d8%a1-%d8%b1%d9%82%d9%85-358-%d9%84%d8%b3%d9%86%d8%a9-2026-%d9%85-%d8%a8%d8%b4%d8%a3%d9%86-%d8%a5%d9%86%d8%b4/>) for a new National Authority for Cybersecurity and Digital Sovereignty. In the last twelve months a wider cybersecurity law has been in preparation. On 15 July 2026 a House committee [met National Security Council officials in Benghazi](<https://alwasat.ly/news/libya/524932>) to work on the bill. No arrest, charge or conviction under the 2022 law has been found. Operating would need a dated arrest, charge, prosecution or conviction, or a penalty.

Cabinet [split the 2024 bill into a Cybercrime Bill 2026 and a Cybersecurity Bill 2026](<https://www.gov.ls/development/stakeholders-engage-on-cybersecurity-bill-2026/>). The Lesotho Times reports that a [2021 version was withdrawn from Parliament](<https://lestimes.com/?p=91666>). It says the 2024 bill was referred but not enacted. In the last twelve months a draft was circulated in August 2026. That month the Director General of ICT said both bills were [ready and waiting for approval by the National Assembly](<https://lesothotribune.co.ls/interim-csirt-lesotho-cybersecurity-launch/>). No cybercrime or cybersecurity law in force has been found. Establishing would need a cybercrime or cybersecurity law in force, as an act of its own or as part of a penal or digital code.

Morocco's [Loi n° 05-20 on cybersecurity](<https://www.anrt.ma/sites/default/files/2022-02/loi_05-20_cybersecurite_fr.pdf>) was promulgated by dahir n° 1-20-69 of 25 July 2020 and published on 6 August 2020. Décret n° 2-24-921, applying article 25, was in force by the Bulletin officiel of 20 February 2025. In the last twelve months, [in November 2026 the National Defence Administration was working on a revision of the law](<https://lematin.ma/nation/cybersecurite-15-centres-de-surveillance-prevus-la-loi-en-revision/376014>). The DGSN [counted 13,643 cybercrime cases in 2025](<https://snrtnews.com/fr/article/cybercriminalite-au-maroc-13643-affaires-liees-aux-technologies-modernes-et-au-chantage>) and 415 arrests. Neither figure names the 2020 law. Operating would need a dated arrest, charge, prosecution or conviction naming the law, or a penalty.

Madagascar's cybercrime framework [still rests in part on loi n°2014-006, adopted in June 2014](<https://www.wearetech.africa/fr/fils/actualites/tech/madagascar-actualise-son-arsenal-face-a-la-montee-des-risques-numeriques>). In the last twelve months, on 8 January 2026 the Presidency [said prosecutions were under way](<https://fr.allafrica.com/stories/202601090348.html>) for online insults. It recalled article 20 of that law. The Council of Ministers [adopted a bill recasting the law](<https://www.2424.mg/cadre-juridique-le-gouvernement-propose-une-mise-a-jour-de-la-loi-sur-la-lutte-contre-la-cybercriminalite/>) on 7 July 2026. In November 2026 the government [withdrew it from the Assembly's agenda](<https://www.lexpress.mg/2026/11/telecommunications-le-gouvernement.html>). No source found shows the 2014 law in regular use in the last two years. Mature would need sources from the past two years that show it used again and again.

IPI states that Mali [amended its Penal Code in December 2024](<https://ipi.media/mali-military-junta-uses-cybercrime-provisions-to-target-journalists/>), incorporating provisions previously in the 2019 cybercrime law. In the last twelve months, Human Rights Watch reports that editor Youssouf Sissoko was [arrested on 5 February 2026](<https://www.hrw.org/news/2026/02/09/press-freedom-under-fire-in-mali>) under the 2019 law. RSF says he was [sentenced on 23 March 2026 to two years in prison](<https://rsf.org/en/broadcast-suspension-and-arrests-journalists-mali-nearly-six-years-transition-marked-repression>). The criminal chamber of the cybercrime pole [had 4 cases involving 8 accused](<https://www.lessor.ml/posts/pole-de-lutte-contre-la-cybercriminalite-le-ministre-kassogue-salue-loperationnalisation-de-la-chambre-criminelle-6a0efcf332029>) on 21 May 2026. Journalist Chahana Takiou was [sentenced on 3 August 2026 to 12 months, 6 suspended](<https://lessor.ml/posts/mali-le-journaliste-chahana-takiou-ecope-dune-peine-de-12-mois-dont-6-avec-sursis-6a70f92a500ac>). The trial of commentator Mohamed Youssouf Bathily [began on 10 August 2026](<https://ipi.media/mali-military-junta-uses-cybercrime-provisions-to-target-journalists/>).

INTIC says Law 13/2026 on cybersecurity and Law 14/2026 on cybercrime [entered into force on 29 September 2026](<https://intic.gov.mz/mocambique-eleito-para-o-comite-de-gestao-da-anca-cert-em-representacao-da-africa-austral/>). Before them, the Penal Code (Law 24/2019, amended by Law 17/2020) [also defined cybercrimes](<https://www.dlapiperdataprotection.com/guide.pdf?c=MZ>). In the last twelve months, Parliament [unanimously approved the Cyber Security Law in April 2026](<https://clubofmozambique.com/news/mozambique-parliament-unanimously-approves-cyber-security-law/>), and President Chapo [promulgated it](<https://clubofmozambique.com/news/mozambique-cybercrime-and-cybersecurity-laws-national-payments-system-law-signed-into-force/>) in June 2026. No arrest, charge, prosecution, conviction or penalty under the laws has been found in the last three years. Operating would need a dated arrest, charge, prosecution or conviction, or a penalty.

Mauritania's [Law no. 2016-007 on cybercrime](<https://mtnima.gov.mr/sites/default/files/loi_2016_-_007_relative_la_cybercriminalite.pdf>) was adopted by the National Assembly and the Senate and promulgated by the President of the Republic. It has 52 articles covering offences, search and interception powers, and international cooperation. No change to the law has been found in the last twelve months. No arrest, charge, prosecution, conviction or penalty has been found in the last three years. Operating would need a dated arrest, charge, prosecution or conviction, or a penalty.

Mauritius's [Cybersecurity and Cybercrime Act 2021](<https://mauritiusassembly.govmu.org/mauritiusassembly/wp-content/uploads/2023/03/act1621.pdf>) was assented to on 24 November 2021 and proclaimed in force on 10 December 2021. In the last twelve months, [regulations designating critical information infrastructure](<https://mitci.govmu.org/mitci/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/113_The-Cybersecurity-and-Cybercrime_Critical-Information-Infrastructure-Designation_Reg-2026.pdf>) came into operation under it in June 2026. On 10 November 2026 the ministry said amendments had [gone to the Attorney-General's Office for vetting](<https://mitci.govmu.org/mitci/national-campaign-promotes-responsible-use-of-social-media/>). The police Cybercrime Unit [handled 930 cases from January 2023 to January 2026](<https://www.lemauricien.com/actualites/faits-divers/escroqueries-et-fraudes-en-ligne-plus-de-900-affaires-traitees-en-3-ans-pour-130-arrestations/700378/>), with 130 arrests. The source does not name the Act. Operating would need a dated arrest, charge, prosecution or conviction naming the law, or a penalty.

Malawi's Electronic Transactions and Cyber Security Act, Act 33 of 2016, [was gazetted on 4 November 2016 and commenced on 1 June 2017](<https://malawilii.org/akn/mw/act/2016/33/eng@2017-12-31>). In the last twelve months, in October 2026 the Justice Minister [said a new cybercrime bill](<https://www.nyasatimes.com/malawi-pushes-tough-new-laws-to-track-expose-and-jail-online-scammers/>) should go to Parliament in the February to April 2027 session. Nyasa Times reports that Collins Magalasi was [charged in court in September 2026](<https://www.nyasatimes.com/magalasi-charged-with-hacking-malawi-presidents-phone-and-senior-officials-numbers/>) under section 83(1), read with section 89. The charge is aiding the hacking of the President's phone. In August 2024 police [charged a Mzuzu man with cyber spamming](<https://mwnation.com/divisive-war-on-cybercrimes/>) under section 91. Mature would need sources from the past two years that show it used again and again.

In December 2024 the regulator CRAN [said Namibia lacks dedicated cybercrime legislation](<https://namibiadailynews.info/cran-and-nam-csirt-tackle-ransomware-attack-on-telecom-operator/>). Namibia's proposed cybercrime law is the Cybercrime Bill. In the last twelve months, a draft bill [was presented to stakeholders in Windhoek](<https://www.thevillager.com.na/national/2026/cybercrime-bill-in-the-pipeline-for-namibia/>) on 18 February 2026, and in April 2026 [the final draft was circulated ahead of a validation workshop](<https://www.namibian.com.na/problems-with-the-cybercrime-bill/>), before it goes to Parliament. No cybercrime or cybersecurity law in force has been found. Establishing would need a cybercrime or cybersecurity law in force, as an act of its own or as part of a penal or digital code.

Niger's cybercrime law is law no. 2019-33 of 3 July 2019. It was [amended on 12 June 2024](<https://www.lesahel.org/lutte-contre-la-cybercriminalite-la-police-judiciaire-face-aux-nouvelles-technologies-de-linformation/>) to set penalties for online defamation, insults and harmful data. In the last twelve months, on 3 December 2025 the State Court [upheld journalist Samira Sabou's 2020 conviction](<https://cpj.org/2026/01/niger-arrests-dw-correspondent-over-report-on-nigerian-refugees/>) and ruled that the law applied. On 13 October 2026 the Niamey High Court [convicted the lawyer Lirwana under Article 31](<https://eusee.hivos.org/alert/arrest-and-subsequent-conviction-of-human-rights-defender-and-lawyer-lirwana-abdourahmane-for-social-media-post/>). It sentenced him to two years and a 2 million CFA franc fine. No source found shows the law in regular use in the last two years. Mature would need sources from the past two years that show it used again and again.

Nigeria's Cybercrimes (Prohibition, Prevention, etc.) Act is [an enacted law of 2015](<https://www.dataphyte.com/topic/technology/who-protects-nigerias-digital-citizens/>). The President signed an amendment in February 2024, after [the Senate passed it in December 2023 and the House on 14 February 2024](<https://placng.org/Legist/cybercrimes-amendment-act-exposes-lapses-in-legislative-process/>). In December 2024 activist Olamide Thomas was [arrested and charged over a Facebook post](<https://www.vanguardngr.com/2025/08/how-misuse-of-cybercrime-act-cost-nigeria-n1-1trn-in-7-yrs/>). In the last twelve months the Department of State Services has been prosecuting activist Omoyele Sowore. [On 30 August 2026 its Director-General said the prosecution would wait until after the 2027 election](<https://punchng.com/sowore-serap-lawyer-demand-dss-withdraw-charges/>). On 15 October 2026 the Southern Africa Litigation Centre said that [section 24 is repeatedly used to arrest journalists](<https://www.southernafricalitigationcentre.org/oral-statement-under-item-3-the-human-rights-situation-in-africa/>).

On 5 June 2025 Rwanda's Supreme Court [upheld the constitutionality of Article 39](<https://monitor.civicus.org/explore/opposition-leader-victoire-ingabire-re-arrested-court-ruling-deals-blow-to-freedom-of-expression/>) of the 2018 Cybercrime Law, CIVICUS Monitor reports. The article criminalises publishing rumours through digital platforms. In the last twelve months the law was cited and not changed: a commentary of 30 July 2026 in the East African Policy Observer says that [Rwanda's binding legal instruments include cybersecurity law](<https://eastafricanpolicyobserver.org/commentary/new-africa-tech-policy-insights-on-nigeria-rwanda-and-zambia-ictworks/>). The ruling records no arrest, charge or conviction under the law, and none has been found in the last three years. Operating would need a dated arrest, charge, prosecution or conviction, or a penalty.

A rights group says Sudan's Cybercrime Law [was amended in 2018, 2020 and 2022](<https://skylineforhuman.org/en/news/details/875/sudans-draconian-cybercrime-law-amendments-pose-grave-threat-to-digital-freedoms>). It says the Cabinet approved a further draft amendment on 13 October 2025. In the last twelve months, on 21 July 2026 the Red Sea State cybercrime prosecutor [issued 17 arrest warrants](<https://rsf.org/en/sudan-army-backed-authorities-are-prosecuting-15-journalists-and-two-media-outlets-under-anti>), RSF reports. They name 15 journalists and two news sites. In August 2026 a criminal court in El Obeid [sentenced pharmacist Ahmed Suleiman Ahmed Al-Waqi to six years](<https://thesudantimes.com/sudan/sudanese-army-accused-of-using-courts-to-silence-anti-war-voices/>), three of them under the law. On 1 November 2026 the Council of Ministers [approved a draft Cybersecurity Regulation Bill 2026](<https://suna.sd/posts/mgls-alozraaa-ydyn-alaaatdaaaat-almtkrr-aal-almnshat-alkhdmy-aabr-almsyrat-alty-tntlk-mn-dakhl-dol-athyobya>).

Senegal's cybercrime law is [Law 2008-10 of 25 January 2008](<https://www.mondaq.com/data-protection/693598/data-security-and-cybercrime-in-senegal>). A 2018 practitioner source says no separate cybersecurity act had been adopted. In the last twelve months, in August 2026 the Ministry of Telecommunications and Digital Economy [submitted a bill to the National Assembly's Intercommission](<https://news.broadcastmediaafrica.com/2026/08/17/senegal-advances-new-cybersecurity-bill-to-protect-critical-infrastructure-and-strengthen-digital-sovereignty/>). It would set up a National Cybersecurity Authority and CERTs. Senegal's national police [recorded 3,902 cybercrime complaints in 2024](<https://infosdujour.sn/lutte-contre-la-cybercriminalite-la-police-nationale-enregistre-3-902-plaintes-en-2024-194-personnes-defer/>) and referred 194 people to prosecutors. No source found shows the law in regular use in the last two years. Mature would need sources from the past two years that show it used again and again.

Sierra Leone's [Cyber Security and Crime Act, 2021](<https://sierralii.gov.sl/akn/sl/act/2021/7/eng@2021-11-25/source.pdf>) was published as a supplement to the Gazette dated 25 November 2021. It sets up a response coordination centre, an advisory council and a fund, and defines offences. No change has been found in the last twelve months. A Freetown councillor was [charged at Pademba Road Court in November 2025](<https://sierraloaded.sl/local/councillor-court-alleged-cyber-charges-mp/>) with cyberstalking and cyberbullying, and Joseph Sesay was [arraigned at the same court](<https://www.premiermedia-sl.com/man-arraigned-for-alleged-cyberbullying-in-freetown/>) on 5 August 2025. No source found shows the law in regular use in the last two years. Mature would need sources from the past two years that show it used again and again.

The [National Communications Authority](<https://nca.gov.so/somalias-parliament-approves-the-cybersecurity-law/>) states that the House of the People approved the Cybersecurity Law on 26 January 2026. In the last twelve months, the House [concluded first reading](<https://moct.gov.so/en/%F0%9D%97%99%F0%9D%97%9C%F0%9D%97%A5%F0%9D%97%A6%F0%9D%97%A7-%F0%9D%97%A5%F0%9D%97%98%F0%9D%97%94%F0%9D%97%97%F0%9D%97%9C%F0%9D%97%A1%F0%9D%97%9A-%F0%9D%97%A2%F0%9D%97%99-%F0%9D%97%A7%F0%9D%97%9B/>) of the Cybercrimes Bill on 8 December 2025. On 29 August 2026 the Senate [held first reading](<https://www.dawan.africa/news/somalia-senate-holds-first-reading-of-cybersecurity-meteorological-agency-bills>) of a 33-article cybersecurity bill, which still needs second and third readings. No cybercrime or cybersecurity law in force has been found. Establishing would need a cybercrime or cybersecurity law in force, as an act of its own or as part of a penal or digital code.

Parliament had [passed the bill](<https://www.radiotamazuj.org/en/news/article/south-sudan-parliament-passes-controversial-cybercrime-bill>) on 25 November 2025. No arrest, charge, prosecution, conviction or penalty under the law has been found. Operating would need a dated arrest, charge, prosecution or conviction, or a penalty.

Sao Tome and Principe's [Lei n.º 15/2017, the Lei sobre Cibercrime](<https://natlex.ilo.org/dyn/natlex2/natlex2/files/download/110002/152017.pdf>), was passed by the Assembleia Nacional on 28 June 2017, promulgated on 3 August 2017 and published on 6 October 2017. It creates computer-crime offences and procedural powers, and gives the Polícia Judiciária a contact point open twenty-four hours a day. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No arrest, charge, prosecution, conviction or penalty has been found in the last three years. Operating would need a dated arrest, charge, prosecution or conviction, or a penalty.

Eswatini's [Computer Crime and Cybercrime Act, 2022](<https://www.gov.sz/images/ICT/COMPUTER-CRIME--CYBERCRIME-ACT.pdf>) was published in the Government Gazette on 4 March 2022 and came into operation that day. In the last twelve months it was cited and not changed. In April 2026 the minister [called it the legal groundwork](<https://swazi24.com/44934/news/maziya-opens-push-for-national-data-policy/>), with its regulations at an advanced stage. A Mbabane woman was [convicted by the Magistrates Court in August 2025](<https://swazi24.com/20604/news/crime-and-courts/whatsapp-insult-lands-woman-in-jail/>) over a WhatsApp message. Two accused [appeared in Manzini Magistrates Court](<https://swazidailynews.com/2537/national/two-alleged-facata-scammers-arrested-for-defrauding-victims-over-e80-000/>) in September 2025 on fraud charges, some under the Act. No source found shows the law in regular use in the last two years. Mature would need sources from the past two years that show it used again and again.

Seychelles' [Cybercrimes and Other Related Crimes Act 2021](<https://www.gazette.sc/sites/default/files/2021-12/Act%2059%20-%20Cybercrimes%20and%20other%20Related%20Crimes%20Act%202021.pdf>) (Act 59 of 2021) was assented on 15 December 2021 and repeals the Computer Misuse Act (Cap 254). In the last twelve months, [Act 23 of 2025](<https://www.gazette.sc/sites/default/files/2025-12/Act%2023%202025%20-%20Cybercrimes%20and%20other%20Related%20Crimes%20%28Amendment%29%20Act%202025.pdf>) amended it: the National Assembly passed the amendment on 15 December 2025 and the President assented on 22 December 2025. Operating would need a dated arrest, charge, prosecution or conviction, or a penalty.

The sector regulator ARCEP's [register of laws](<https://arcep.td/lois.html>) lists Loi N°009/PR/2015 on Cybersecurity and the Fight Against Cybercrime among Chad's laws. In the last twelve months, on 16 February 2026 the National Assembly [approved, by 160 votes to 1, the ratification of Ordinance 001/PR/2026 of 22 January 2026](<https://tchadvision.com/lassemblee-nationale-approuve-la-reforme-de-lansice-un-pas-vers-le-numerique-de-demain/>). The ordinance reforms the agency ANSICE to modernise the legal framework on cybersecurity and cybercrime. No arrest, charge, prosecution, conviction or penalty has been found in the last three years. Togo's [Loi n° 2018-026 of 7 December 2018](<https://jo.gouv.tg/sites/default/files/JO/JOS_07_12_2018-63E%20ANNEE%20N%C2%B024TER.pdf>) on cybersecurity and the fight against cybercrime defines and punishes cybercrime offences. [Loi n° 2022-009 of 24 June 2022](<https://ancy.gouv.tg/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/Loi-n%C2%B0-2022-009-portant-modification-de-la-loi-n%C2%B0-2018-026-du-07-decembre-sur-la-cybersecurite-et-la-lutte-.pdf>) amends its articles 2, 3 and 6. The visas of [Décret n° 2022-094/PR of 9 September 2022](<https://monidentite.anid.gouv.tg/documents/d/anid_pub/pr-decret-n-2022-094-pr-relatif-aux-modalites-d-inscription-de-rectification-et-d-actualisation-des-donnees-demographiques-et-biometriques-des-personnes-physiques>) cite both laws as current. Tunisia's [Decree-law no. 2023-17 of 11 March 2023 on cybersecurity](<https://legislation-securite.tn/latest-laws/decret-loi-n-2023-17-du-11-mars-2023-relatif-a-la-cybersecurite/>) sets audit, labelling, classification, incident-response and critical-infrastructure duties. Fines run from 50,000 to 100,000 dinars. Decree-law 54 of September 2022 makes spreading falsehoods by electronic means an offence. The journalists' union SNJT [recorded six prosecutions of journalists under Decree 54](<https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/10/2/tunisia-softens-its-false-news-penalty-what-really-changed-and-why-now>) between April 2025 and April 2026. In the last twelve months, an amendment [replacing jail with fines of 10,000 to 20,000 dinars](<https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/10/2/tunisia-softens-its-false-news-penalty-what-really-changed-and-why-now>) for a first offence took effect on 30 September 2026.

Tanzania's [Cybercrimes Act, Chapter 443 in the Revised Edition 2023, originally Act No. 14 of 2015](<https://www.nps.go.tz/uploads/documents/sw-1751202044-The%20Cybercrimes%20Act.pdf>), commenced on 1 September 2015. It applies to Mainland Tanzania and Zanzibar. In the last twelve months it was cited and not changed. The ICT Minister [said on 19 August 2026](<https://dailynews.co.tz/tanzania-orders-operators-of-critical-ict-infrastructure-to-exercise-greater-vigilance-or-else-face-100m-fine/>) that section 29 sets penalties for damaging critical ICT infrastructure. They are a fine of not less than 100m/- or three times the damage, imprisonment of at least five years, or both. No arrest, charge, prosecution, conviction or penalty has been found in the last three years. Operating would need a dated arrest, charge, prosecution or conviction, or a penalty.

Nilepost says Uganda's cyber-offence framework is [anchored in the Computer Misuse Act, 2011 as amended in 2022](<https://nilepost.co.ug/news/368071/three-arrested-over-alleged-fake-news-personal-data-offences-on-social-media>), in an account dated 1 September 2026. The Constitutional Court [struck down Sections 11, 23, 26, 27, 28 and 29 of the Act](<https://www.newvision.co.ug/category/news/constitutional-court-nullifies-key-computer-m-NV_230010_042026>), leaving the rest standing. No other change has been found in the last twelve months. In September 2026 Kampala Metropolitan Police arrested and held three men over alleged fake news and unlawful disclosure of personal data on social media, and charges were not disclosed. No source found shows the law in regular use in the last two years. Mature would need sources from the past two years that show it used again and again.

South Africa's [Cybercrimes Act 19 of 2020 was signed on 26 May 2021](<https://www.michalsons.com/focus-areas/cybersecurity-law/cybersecurity-bill-in-south-africa-overview>) and [came partly into operation on 1 December 2021](<https://www.itweb.co.za/article/calls-for-finalisation-of-cyber-security-bill/G98YdMLGkRW7X2PD>). [A parliamentary reply of 29 November 2024](<https://www.protectionweb.co.za/cyber-security/specialist-police-investigate-cyber-fraud-prosecutions-remain-low/>) put 37 cases with 88 charges under the Act on court rolls. In the last twelve months, [the Acting Minister of Police told Parliament in October 2026](<https://pmg.org.za/committee-question/41149/>) that the Hawks had registered eight cyber fraud, extortion and ransomware cases over three years. They had made one arrest. No separate cybersecurity act exists, and [in October 2025 a Hawks cybercrime head said a Cybersecurity Bill was still to come](<https://www.gcis.gov.za/newsroom/media-releases/government-urges-vigilance-against-rising-cyber-threats>).

Zambia has a Cyber Crimes Act and a Cyber Security Act, both of 2025. [The Global Network Initiative says the President signed both into law on 8 April 2025](<https://globalnetworkinitiative.org/gni-statement-on-zambias-new-cyber-laws-a-blow-to-freedom-of-expression-and-privacy/>). He had recorded a private conversation during the August 2026 elections. No source found shows the law in regular use in the last two years. Mature would need sources from the past two years that show it used again and again.
